title: Three-month Focus & Cadence Proposal
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a working proposal for a pragmatic three-month company focus and the operational cadence to support predictable progress. It is intentionally compact — we want a small set of cross-org priorities, a tightened cadence for syncs/reports, and a short list of asks for each team ahead of the all-hands in two weeks.

High-level ask:
- Agree to 3 company priorities for the next 90 days (not more).
- Adopt a lightweight weekly cadence for updates (2 slides per team + one line risk).
- Commit team-level OKR drafts by Nov 18 so exec can finalize for all-hands.

Proposed company priorities (90d):
1) Latency & cost-led performance sweep (hosted + dedicated): reduce p50 API latency by 10% and hosted per-token cost by 12% through batching, kernel tuning, and cache improvements.
   - Why: Most customers cite cost/latency tradeoffs as gating for adoption.
   - Success metric: p50 latency drop, hosted per-token $ reduction, three customer pilots showing 10–20% RU improvements.

2) Private deployment readiness: ship VPC onboarding playbook + two pilot customers on Private (VPC/on-prem) with 99.9% uptime for pilot period.
   - Why: Enterprise pipeline increasingly requires Private; pipeline velocity matters to ARR.
   - Success metric: onboarding playbook published, two pilots completing production runbooks.

3) Developer experience & observability: reduce mean time to diagnose by 30% and roll out cost/latency token-level traces to all customers on Dedicated.
   - Why: Customer feedback: hard to debug regressions across model variants and routes.
   - Success metric: MTTD metric improvements, usage of tracing dashboard, three regressions detected earlier in the period.

Top-level timeline (90 days):
- Week 0 (now): finalize company priorities and publish this cadence proposal.
- Week 1–2: teams submit team-level draft OKRs and two-slide weekly update templates.
- Week 2: company all-hands (orientation + priority deep dives) — ask each lead to present 5-min priority plan.
- Week 3–12: weekly slot for exec sync (30m) + cross-functional triage office hours (1h) for blockers.
- Week 6: mid-point review & risk reset (all-hands lightning update).
- Week 12: outcome review + learnings + next 90d planning.

Proposed cadence and artifacts:
- Weekly (every Mon): Teams post a 2-slide update to a shared folder by 10:00am PT. Slide format: 1) progress vs key results (one chart/metric), 2) current blocker + one ask. Also add a one-line risk statement in the doc title.
- Exec sync (Wed 9:30am PT, 30m): quick highlights from 3 teams (pre-rotating).
- Triage office hours (Fri 11am PT): open table for infra/capacity/customer escalations.
- Mid-point micro-all-hands (Week 6): 20-min town check-in, 5 quick demos.

Draft company-level OKRs (for feedback):
Objective A: Deliver a materially faster and cheaper hosted API.
  KR1: Reduce p50 text-generation latency from X ms to X - 10% across top-5 models by end of quarter.
  KR2: Reduce hosted per-token cost by 12% (measured on production user mix).
  KR3: Automated prefix/KV cache adoption in top-3 customer verticals.

Objective B: Make Private deployments frictionless for early enterprise customers.
  KR1: Publish VPC onboarding playbook + runbook with clear team-level steps.
  KR2: Complete two pilot Private onboardings with SLA playbooks and measurable latency baselines.
  KR3: Integrate KMS flow with at least one major cloud provider and document HSM fallback.

Objective C: Raise developer productivity and reduce MTTD on regressions.
  KR1: Ship token-level tracing feature to Dedicated customers with docs and 2 example dashboards.
  KR2: Reduce average incident-to-diagnosis time by 30% for production inference incidents.
  KR3: Create a regression-detection runbook + 3 evaluated prompt sets for daily checks.

All-hands planning (two-weeks out):
- Format: 90 minutes. 15-min leadership context, 30-min two deep dives (priority owners), 25-min breakouts (product/eng/customer success), 15-min Q&A + asks.
- Prep deliverables due Nov 18: 5-min synopses from priority owners (one slide each), two demo artifacts (short recordings or screenshots), and 3 customer signals that validate urgency.
- Moderation: CEO opening, Head of Eng priority owner, Head of Product closing call-to-action.

Template for team OKR submissions (deadline Nov 18):
- Team name
- 1–2 objectives aligned to company priorities or supporting product/ops health
- 3 key results per objective (metric + baseline + target)
- Top 3 milestones + owners
- Risks & mitigation (one line each)

Risks and mitigations (initial):
- Risk: Too many cross-cutting asks -> diffusion of focus.
  Mitigation: Enforce 3 company priorities; any add-on must be justified and signed off by exec.
- Risk: Infra capacity constraints during latency sweep may impact customers.
  Mitigation: Temporary routing policies and staged canaries; maintain a fallback variant list.
- Risk: Private pilot delays due to legal/KYC.
  Mitigation: Engage Legal/PS early, pre-validate contract templates.

Asks of teams before Nov 18:
- Eng: concrete latency experiments + quick load budget for canaries (estimates due Nov 12).
- Infra/SRE: capacity headroom plan for staged rollouts; list of gating incidents (Nov 14).
- Product: customer evidence briefs and prioritized pilot list.
- CS/SEs: customer outreach plan and pilot support schedule.

Decision points for execs this week:
1) Lock the 3 company priorities (yes/no).
2) Approve the cadence and weekly update format.
3) Confirm all-hands format and owners.

Open questions:
- Do we want to include a bucket for strategic R&D (1x lower priority) with a funding guardrail?
- Should we mandate a cross-team QA pass for any change that touches routing/policy?

Next steps (owner):
- This doc: finalize and send to execs for thumbs-up by Nov 6 (Avery).
- Templates and slide skeleton: design/ops to publish Nov 7 (Elena + Marcus).
- Teams: draft OKRs in drive by Nov 18 (team leads).

Notes to reviewers / style:
- This is a working document; please use inline comments in the drive copy rather than editing raw text.
- Short, measurable, and time-boxed wins beat laundry lists. If something cannot get to a metric within 90 days, consider a milestone instead.

Contact: Avery Kim (avery.kim@redwood.ai) for questions or if your team needs a one-off extension.

Revision history:
- v0.1 (2025-11-03) initial draft.
- v0.2 (2025-11-08) added OKR wording + all-hands agenda per exec feedback.
- v0.3 (2025-11-12) tightened weekly cadence and added triage hours.
